description: Fix non-interactive cam init hang: ask()/askChoice() now resolve to a default on readline EOF/close, and the build-release smoke supplies --merge-mode (CAM-101 regression).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: The 'close' event fires when the input stream emits 'end' (EOF), or on Ctrl-D/Ctrl-C, or on rl.close(). The callback-API rl.question(cb) callback does NOT fire on EOF before a line is entered. Recommended non-interactive pattern: register rl.on('close') and resolve to a default if not already answered.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/commands/setup.ts:68]: collectViaReadline still hangs in the real non-interactive path when more than one init option is undefined on a single stdin stream. The new rl.on('close') guard only fires for the FIRST readline interface; subsequent interfaces created on the already-ended stream never receive 'close' (node:readline docs: 'close' fires only when input RECEIVES its 'end' event, which a pre-ended stream does not re-emit). Reproduced: collectViaReadline({}, eofStream) hangs >4s. This contradicts US-001's description ('collectViaReadline never hangs') and the PRD goal ('Fix non-interactive cam init hang'). The build smoke is saved only because US-002 supplies every flag (early-return before readline). Mechanical 1-file fix: in ask(), short-circuit to defaultValue when input.readableEnded is already true (or resolve all remaining prompts to defaults after the first EOF).

userStories.title: Resolve ask()/askChoice() to a default on readline EOF/close
userStories.description: As a cam init caller running non-interactively (CI, piped, closed stdin), I need ask()/askChoice() to resolve to the supplied default when stdin reaches EOF so that collectViaReadline never hangs waiting on a line event that will never arrive.
acceptanceCriteria: ask() accepts a default value and, when stdin emits 'close'/EOF before any line is entered, resolves to that default instead of hanging. [oracle: bun test]
askChoice() resolves to its defaultChoice when stdin emits 'close'/EOF before any line is entered. [oracle: bun test]

A guard flag (e.g. an 'answered' boolean) ensures a normal line answer still wins on the happy path and the later close-driven resolve is a harmless no-op (existing happy-path behavior is preserved byte-for-byte). [oracle: bun test]
A unit test drives ask() with a stdin-like stream that ends immediately (EOF) and asserts the call resolves to the default and does not hang. [oracle: bun test]
A unit test drives askChoice() with a stream that ends immediately (EOF) and asserts the call resolves to the defaultChoice and does not hang. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Root fix. File: src/commands/setup.ts. `ask` at ~line 68 (uses rl.question callback at :71); `askChoice` at ~line 78; both build a node:readline interface via createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout }) at :69. The callback API rl.question(cb) fires ONLY on a complete 'line' event; on EOF (piped /dev/null) the stream emits 'end' -> readline emits 'close' but the question callback NEVER fires, so the Promise never resolves -> infinite hang. Fix: register rl.on('close', ...) that resolves to the supplied default if not already answered. ask() currently takes no default and is module-private; the implementer must let ask() accept/return a default and make ask()/askChoice() reachable from a test (export them or inject a stdin stream) — testing strategy is the implementer's call. Match existing test conventions in test/setup-prompt.test.ts (bun:test, import from ../src/commands/setup.ts). Do not change the happy-path line-event path. Per project CLAUDE.md: keep changes surgical; success/failure UX is the print path here (readline), not Ink.

userStories.title: Deterministic guard test: readline collection flow resolves init defaults on EOF, never hangs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a bun test that drives the readline collection seam with a closed/EOF input stream and asserts it resolves (timeout-bounded) to the 'immediate' merge_mode default, so that any future regression of the EOF-hang (or a new mandatory init answer without a flag) fails CI deterministically without depending on claude being installed.
acceptanceCriteria: A new bun test drives the readline collection seam (collectViaReadline, or collectSetupAnswers called with mergeMode undefined so needsMerge=true forces the readline path) with a closed/EOF input stream, exercising the exact prompt path the build smoke triggers. [oracle: bun test]

The test is timeout-bounded (e.g. AbortSignal.timeout or a manual timer that fails the test in the 5-15s range) and FAILS if the collection call does not resolve before the timeout (proving no hang). [oracle: bun test]

On EOF the test asserts the resolved mergeMode equals 'immediate' (the same default readMergeMode returns at src/config/models.ts:138), proving the integration returns the defaults on EOF. [oracle: bun test]

The test runs identically on CI: it does NOT spawn the binary, does NOT require claude to be installed, and keys NO skip on claude-absence or any external tool (it never reaches verifyAgent at src/commands/setup.ts:517). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: New test file (mirror test/setup-prompt.test.ts conventions: bun:test, import from ../src/commands/setup.ts). Do NOT spawn the binary: runSetup calls verifyAgent() at src/commands/setup.ts:517 and `return 1` at :521 BEFORE collectSetupAnswers at :525, and CI (.github/workflows, macos-latest) installs bun+tmux but NOT claude, so a binary-spawn approach never reaches the readline EOF path on CI (guard theater). Instead test the collection seam directly: drive collectViaReadline (or collectSetupAnswers with mergeMode undefined so needsMerge=true at setup.ts:105 forces the readline branch at :120) using a closed/EOF input stream. Testability seam: ask/askChoice (and collectViaReadline) should accept an optional input stream defaulting to process.stdin (the same injectable seam US-001 introduces); exact mechanism (export the collector vs. inject the stream) is the implementer's call, but the asserted EOF path MUST run on CI with no claude present. Default merge_mode is 'immediate' (src/config/models.ts:138 readMergeMode default). Keep distinct from US-001: US-001 proves the ask/askChoice primitives resolve on EOF; US-003 proves the integration (collection flow returns mergeMode='immediate' on EOF), the real path the smoke triggers. Depends on US-001 landing first.

findings.text: collectViaReadline still hangs in the real non-interactive path when more than one init option is undefined on a single stdin stream. The new rl.on('close') guard only fires for the FIRST readline interface; subsequent interfaces created on the already-ended stream never receive 'close' (node:readline docs: 'close' fires only when input RECEIVES its 'end' event, which a pre-ended stream does not re-emit). Reproduced: collectViaReadline({}, eofStream) hangs >4s. This contradicts US-001's description ('collectViaReadline never hangs') and the PRD goal ('Fix non-interactive cam init hang'). The build smoke is saved only because US-002 supplies every flag (early-return before readline). Mechanical 1-file fix: in ask(), short-circuit to defaultValue when input.readableEnded is already true (or resolve all remaining prompts to defaults after the first EOF).

The US-003 integration test pre-fills projectMode+issueSystem and leaves only mergeMode undefined, exercising a single-prompt path. It deliberately sidesteps the multi-prompt single-stream hang (documented as a test-only gotcha in patterns.md), which masks the production gap. Add a test driving collectViaReadline({}, eofStream) with all options undefined to lock in the full non-interactive path.

The 'Single-stream EOF reuse gotcha' bullet frames the multi-prompt hang as a test concern only; in production collectViaReadline shares one process.stdin across up to four sequential prompts, so the same hang is reachable via 'cam init </dev/null' with partial flags when claude is installed. Note the production reachability, not just the test workaround.
